answer_to_user:
Quick scope note first: MarketDX has a 'scan everything for a positioning extreme' tool only for the FUTURES/COT (Commitment of Traders) universe — commodities, FX, rates and equity-index futures — not a market-wide scan of single-stock options put/call. (For a specific optionable NAME's put/call, I'd need you to name the ticker; then options_sentiment gives its stretch vs its own 90-day norm.) Here's where the speculative crowd sits at a 3-year extreme RIGHT NOW (≥90th or ≤10th percentile), which is the closest read to 'crowded positioning to know about':

EQUITY INDEX (most relevant to a stock investor):
- Russell 2000 (IWM) e-mini — net -23.5% of OI, 5th percentile (z -1.7): about as net-short as this crowd gets in 3 years (squeeze risk if it turns).
- Nasdaq-100 (QQQ) mini — net -20.7%, 5th percentile (z -1.45): similarly crowded-short.

RATES:
- 2Y UST — net -28%, 100th percentile (z +2.05): about as positioned for LOWER yields as ever.
- SOFR-3M — 5th percentile (z -2.12): crowded the other way (positioned for higher yields).

FX: EUR/USD at the 2nd percentile (crowded short, z -2.4, the single most stretched); AUD (93rd), MXN (96th), BRL (95th) crowded long; CAD (9th) crowded short.

COMMODITIES: Copper (99th, z +1.71), KC wheat (99th), cotton (96th), sugar (91st) crowded LONG; lean hogs (3rd) and orange juice (8th) crowded SHORT.

Read these as contrarian-RISK flags (a crowded trade that could unwind hard on a shock), not buy/sell signals — an extreme can persist. The standouts for an equity investor: small-caps (IWM) and Nasdaq (QQQ) both sit crowded-SHORT near 3-year lows.
